parsed.explanation: Claim 3.2's proof forms the integer π(T) and asks whether it lies in S_∞; this is meaningful only for finite T, so Step 3 establishes hypothesis (iii) only for finite minimal transversals. Step 4's Theorem assumes (iii) for all minimal transversals, and its final contradiction applies (iii) to a minimal transversal T extracted by Zorn from the infinite set I∪Z_ω — T's finiteness is then inferred from T∈C, which is exactly what is unjustified (Case A's impossibility rules out any finite I∪Z_s being a transversal, so the finite version cannot be substituted). Intersecting antichains can have infinite minimal transversals, so this needs a new lemma; without it the finiteness of M (L6.2) is unproved.
